title: Design a Vending Machine
relevance: High — the textbook State-pattern LLD / machine-coding question (campus + experienced); Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Walmart, and Indian product cos use it to probe FSM modeling, inventory + change logic, and concurrency.
company_notes: Campus/machine-coding (Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon new-grad, Indian product cos): common design+code round where working FSM + change + inventory beats a half-finished pattern zoo. Experienced LLD (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Walmart): same core with deeper ExactChangeOnly, jam/refund, integer money, Strategy payment, and stock/vault concurrency probes. Among the top canonical LLD problems; treat as the State-pattern template for later FSM questions (ATM, traffic light, document workflow).

phases.goal: Lock functional scope, clarifying product rules, NFRs, and scale assumptions before any class diagram.

must_hit.point: Mandatory FR: multi-product inventory with prices/qty; accept coins (and often notes); select product; dispense and return change; reject insufficient funds / out-of-stock; cancel yields full refund.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists inventory, coin accept, select, dispense+change, reject paths, and cancel→refund without jumping to code.

must_hit.point: Clarify order and money rules up front: select-then-pay vs pay-then-select; coins only vs notes/card/UPI; exact-change-only when hopper is low; slot codes vs product ids; cancel/refund anytime before dispense; admin restock/collect cash.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate asks clarifying questions and states explicit assumptions rather than silently picking defaults.

must_hit.point: NFR bar: correct state transitions with no charge without dispense; thread-safe stock/cash if concurrent; extensible payment and states; money as integer minor units; working demo/CLI.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions FSM correctness, integer money, extensibility, and optional concurrency without inventing fleet scale.

must_hit.point: State assumptions: one transaction at a time per machine; canonical denominations so greedy change is OK; no networked fleet unless asked; spot/SKU count is tiny so in-memory maps are fine.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States single-session machine, local in-memory inventory, and keeps fleet sync out of the OOD round.

probes: What clarifying questions do you ask before drawing classes?
Is this select-then-pay or pay-then-select, and what happens on cancel?

hints.1: Start from customer and admin use cases, not patterns.
hints.2: Separate mandatory FR (inventory, coins, select, dispense+change, reject, cancel) from extensions (card/UPI, ExactChangeOnly, jam, alerts).
hints.3: Say: one transaction per machine; integer minor units; ask select-then-pay vs pay-then-select and exact-change-only explicitly.

phases.goal: Name the domain objects and session/cash/inventory responsibilities that the FSM will orchestrate.

must_hit.point: Core entities: VendingMachine as context/Facade; VendingMachineState hierarchy; Inventory/Slot plus Product/Item; CashBox/CoinVault holding session insert and change reserve; optional PaymentStrategy, Display Observer, and admin API.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names machine, states, inventory/slots/products, and cash box with session vs reserve, not a single god blob.

must_hit.point: Prefer slot-based inventory (slotId → product + qty + capacity) over a flat product→qty map so restock fills physical slots and the same SKU can span multiple slots.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Models slots with code, product, qty, capacity rather than only a product map.

must_hit.point: Money model: Coin/Note enums with value in cents (or paise); CashBox tracks reserve Map<Coin,int> plus sessionInserted; never float prices/balances.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses integer cents/paise and denomination enums; separates session cash from hopper reserve.

probes: What are the main entities and who owns stock vs change vs session balance?
Why slots instead of a product→quantity map?

hints.1: List nouns from the happy path: machine, item, slot, coin, change.
hints.2: Machine holds state + session; Inventory owns slots; CashBox owns hopper and session insert.
hints.3: Sketch: VendingMachine → Inventory(Slot/Product) + CashBox(session+reserve) + VendingMachineState; optional PaymentStrategy/Display.

phases.goal: Draw the Facade + State hierarchy and public APIs so transitions live in states, not a giant switch.

must_hit.point: VendingMachine holds state, inventory, cashBox, balance/selectedCode/session and exposes insertCoin/selectItem/dispense/refund/setState as the public Facade; it must not become a giant if/else on a state enum.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows context fields and delegates customer ops to current state via setState transitions.

must_hit.point: VendingMachineState abstract/interface with IdleState, HasMoneyState, ItemSelectedState, DispensingState (optional ExactChangeOnly/OutOfStock/Maintenance); each state implements insertCoin/selectItem/dispense/refund and owns transitions via machine.setState.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the state classes and methods; transitions are inside states, not a central switch.

must_hit.point: Supporting APIs: Inventory isAvailable/reduceStock/addItem; CashBox insert/canMakeChange/makeChange/refundSession; customer insertCoin/insertNote, selectItem, dispense, refund/cancel, display; admin restock, collectCash, setExactChangeOnly.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Surfaces inventory and cash-box methods plus customer vs admin APIs matching the skeleton.

probes: Walk me through the class diagram and where transitions live.
What methods does each state need to implement?

hints.1: Draw the FSM happy path before naming classes.
hints.2: Facade delegates to current VendingMachineState; Inventory and CashBox sit beside the context.
hints.3: Idle → HasMoney (or ItemSelected) → Dispensing → Idle with per-state insertCoin/selectItem/dispense/refund and setState inside states.

phases.goal: Implement FSM behavior, integer money, change pre-checks, and atomic commit of stock plus vault.

must_hit.point: Typical happy path Idle → HasMoney (or ItemSelected) → Dispensing → Idle; invalid actions in a state must no-op/error/refund and never silently corrupt balance.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Narrates legal transitions and explicit reject/refund for illegal ops in each state.

must_hit.point: Money is integer cents/paise only; denominations as enums (e.g. Coin.QUARTER = 25); never double/float for prices or balance.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses int minor units and enum coin values; rejects floating-point money.

must_hit.point: Change-making: greedy largest-first against available hopper counts; if exact change impossible, abort sale and refund full insert (or enter ExactChangeOnly); mention DP when denominations are arbitrary.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes hopper-aware greedy, full refund on failure, and DP as the non-canonical follow-up.

must_hit.point: Transaction atomicity: validate stock and canMakeChange(deposit - price) before decrementing inventory or committing coins; on dispense failure, full refund and lock slot.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Pre-checks stock and change, then commits; jam path refunds all and locks the slot.

probes: How do you decide whether you can dispense and return change?
What happens if the dispense motor fails after payment?

hints.1: Implement the happy path states before extensions.
hints.2: Pre-check stock and canMakeChange, then mutate inventory and vault together.
hints.3: Greedy against hopper counts; if change impossible refund full insert; jam → full refund + lock slot, never keep money without an item.

phases.goal: Show OCP/SOLID hooks for new states, payments, and change algorithms without rewriting the Facade.

must_hit.point: State pattern over enum-switch for OCP: adding Maintenance / ExactChangeOnly / Jam should not edit a giant switch in VendingMachine; each new state is a class.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Prefers State classes so new modes plug in without touching a central switch.

must_hit.point: State vs Strategy: State changes with internal mode and triggers the next mode; Strategy is an interchangeable algorithm (change-making, card vs cash) unaware of sibling strategies — PaymentStrategy for card/UPI often skips change.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates FSM states from PaymentStrategy/change Strategy and explains when each applies.

must_hit.point: SOLID signal: OCP for new state/payment/change algo without editing VendingMachine; SRP — state owns transitions, vault owns change, inventory owns stock; DIP on VendingMachineState/PaymentStrategy; Singleton OK for one physical machine but prefer DI for tests / multi-machine.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps OCP/SRP/DIP to concrete types and qualifies Singleton with DI for tests.

probes: How would you add ExactChangeOnly or card/UPI without rewriting VendingMachine?

hints.1: Ask what should change without editing the Facade.
hints.2: New behavior → new State or PaymentStrategy/change Strategy, not more ifs.
hints.3: ExactChangeOnlyState / Maintenance as states; CashPayment vs CardPayment as Strategy; Singleton only for one process↔one machine, inject for tests.

phases.goal: Protect single-machine sessions and atomic stock/vault updates under concurrent UI or admin access.

must_hit.point: One physical machine usually serializes customer sessions with a single transaction lock; still protect stock decrement and cash vault (read-calculate-commit) so admin restock / multi-UI cannot double-vend.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes a session lock plus atomic stock/vault commit so the last unit cannot vend twice.

must_hit.point: Hot path is commit transaction (stock −1 + vault update + change) as one critical section per machine; do not hold the lock during card network I/O — authorize async, then commit.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps the lock around local commit only; card auth stays outside the critical section.

must_hit.point: Admin restock while a sale is in progress: restock only in Idle/Maintenance, or lock inventory mutations against the active transaction; prefer fine-grained locks or ConcurrentHashMap for stock maps if claiming concurrent requests.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Restricts restock to safe states or locks inventory against the active sale.

probes: Two users hit select on the last item — what prevents double vend?
Can admin restock during an active sale?

hints.1: Think one customer session at a time on one machine.
hints.2: Serialize the session and make stock decrement + vault update atomic.
hints.3: Single transaction lock; commit stock−1 and vault together; restock only in Idle/Maintenance or blocked against the active transaction.

tradeoffs.topic: Enum FSM vs State pattern classes
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Enum + switch is faster to code; State classes win OCP when interviewers add Maintenance / ExactChangeOnly / Jam. Prefer State classes in OOD rounds.
Both valid — pick one, draw transitions consistently, and reject the other order in Idle/HasMoney.
Greedy for canonical coin systems against available hopper counts; mention DP (change-making problem) when denominations are arbitrary or hopper constraints break greediness.
OK for one physical device / one process↔one machine; say you’d inject for unit tests or multi-machine simulators and don’t cargo-cult it for fleets.

gotchas.trap: Asking whether selection is allowed before inserting money without stating a product rule
gotchas.correction: Make the rule explicit: either allow ItemSelected then accept coins, or reject until HasMoney.

gotchas.trap: Discovering the machine cannot make change only after mutating stock or committing coins
gotchas.correction: Pre-check canMakeChange; refund all; optionally enter ExactChangeOnlyState.

gotchas.trap: Dispense motor jams after payment and only refunding change or keeping the payment
gotchas.correction: Full refund (not just change), lock the slot, journal the failure; never leave money taken with no item.

gotchas.trap: Two concurrent selects double-vending the last unit
gotchas.correction: Serialize one session lock and atomically decrement stock so two selects cannot vend the last unit twice.

gotchas.trap: Bolting card/UPI into cash state methods
gotchas.correction: Introduce PaymentStrategy; cashless path often skips change and collapses HasMoney self-loops.
Restock only in Idle/Maintenance, or lock inventory mutations against the active transaction.
Interviewer docks the State-pattern signal — transitions belong in state classes via setState.

gotchas.trap: Using double for money or failing to restore hopper coins when change fails mid-calculation
gotchas.correction: Use integer cents/paise only; restore hopper state if change-making aborts.
